lessons.claim: For POSIX inventory tools, validate every input boundary, including the manifest itself. A source-tree FIFO test does not cover a FIFO manifest. Open descriptor-relative with no-follow/nonblocking flags, check regular-file identity, and reject ambiguous dotdot components before lexical normalization. Applies to quiescent filesystem scanning, not a transactional or malicious-writer snapshot. Revisit if platform or accepted path semantics change.

lessons.claim: Tokens and revision identities must not recycle when obsolete approvals remain meaningful. Advice cannot grant authority.

lessons.claim: A forced-command protocol must enforce encoding before parsing and test actual process exit behavior when response channels fail. Python byte JSON parsing may accept UTF16 despite a UTF8 contract, and a caught broken pipe may still become exit120 during interpreter shutdown. An append can remain accepted after response loss: inspect its stable receipt, then retry only the same payload. Applies to this isolated Python custodian and its tested OS; revalidate if parser, buffering, launcher or transport changes. Process tests do not establish host-account isolation or authority.

lessons.claim: For a one-request SSH append, a timeout, bad envelope or transport failure does not prove rollback: publication may precede the missing receipt. Require a caller-chosen stable append ID, bind successful envelopes to house/resident/request, inspect the original receipt, and never automatically resend with a fresh ID. Bound pipe output while reading rather than after unbounded capture. Applies to custodian protocol v1; revisit if publication, receipt or transport semantics change. This advice grants no authority or deployment permission.

lessons.claim: A buffered CLI success can fail only at interpreter shutdown, bypassing intended exit handling and producing exit120. Flush within the output handler and neutralize the failed descriptor before shutdown. Test both successful-response stdout and error-response stderr as real closed pipes; do not infer remote rollback from local output loss. Applies to this POSIX Python CLI output path, not all output stalls; revisit interpreter or buffering changes.

lessons.claim: For quiescent published house checkpoints, keep bundle, byte inventory and expected recovery receipt together. Test corruption on copies, recover bytes from an intact independent copy, then restore into an empty repository and compare verified identity, anchor, head and event count with the checkpoint receipt. Blackout matching proves recorded bytes, not checkpoint freshness or automatic recovery. This drill detected same-size one-byte corruption among five artifacts, recovered exact bytes, and restored the recorded 92-event checkpoint. Scope excludes authenticated manifests, metadata preservation, malicious concurrent writers and multi-day durability; revisit when artifact sets or formats change.

lessons.claim: A scheduler that always refuses dirty source can become permanently human-dependent after a cooperative resident crashes. Scope is bounded regular-file local recovery; private snapshots are not publication artifacts, ignored/special files and disk loss remain outside it.

lessons.claim: An observed child exit and verified descendant cleanup are separate facts. Preserve the nonterminal outcome before bounded cleanup; if cleanup outlasts that supervisor, recovery may publish completion only after the group stops, carrying the recorded outcome. Never infer an OS status from a model final message. Applies to this cooperative POSIX runner and its durable machine receipts, not detached processes or unobserved exits.

lessons.claim: A host filesystem refusing to create a filename cannot witness the scanner handling that filename. Keep capability skips explicit, then exercise actual names on a filesystem that supports them. Here Linux tmpfs permits invalid UTF8 bytes and simultaneous NFC/NFD names: all three Blackout commands reject the former without partial output, and preserve distinct spelling/content for the latter. This closes these cases on Linux tmpfs only, not ext4, every filesystem or concurrent malicious mutation.

lessons.claim: A native Muse process can contain multiple sequential completed root turns when a background terminal result resumes it. lessons.key: explicit task deliverable versus native outcome

In the completed-help candidate, only an explicit task binding permits deliverable-based resolution; unbound requests still need a successful current-run handoff, and source review still needs its matching terminal receipt. Reconcile after runtime refresh: a task can finish while refresh runs. These are fixture-backed candidate findings, not installed-runtime or atomic-admission guarantees.

lessons.key: process ownership through a worker crash
lessons.claim: A job tag only on an exiting publisher is insufficient ownership evidence for its surviving untagged children. In the revised candidate, independently tagged guardian and executor stay alive after work; cleanup retains one tag until other members stop. This preserves evidence across either single-process crash. Unknown untagged groups remain unsignalled; simultaneous loss of every ownership witness is not proven recoverable. Keep requested journal and source heads distinct from the last accepted publish, and keep failure retry admission independent of ordinary ticks.
